title: When the Ember Sings
premise: Lena Joubert has survived twelve years in the city of Verrance by carving bone charms that whisper only to her, hiding the gift she inherited from the grandmother who taught her to listen. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning anyone who hears the dead, Lena is betrayed by a customer and dragged before King Aldric—only to discover the king himself is possessed by an ancient ember-spirit that feeds on memory, and that he secretly begs her for help. To free him, Lena must unbind the spirit using the one thing it cannot digest: willingly given memories, offered up by the found family of outcasts she gathers along the way. In the end, Lena sacrifices her own recollection of her grandmother to sing the ember back into sleep, saving the king but losing the past—and choosing, with her new family beside her, to build memories worth keeping.
about_author: Paloma Whitlock is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring carved bone artifacts and wondering what they remembered. She writes quiet, grief-haunted fantasy from a drafty house full of rescued cats.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: In Lena's POV, we see her careful double life: carving charms by day, listening to grateful ghosts by night, and dodging the crown's new edict. A dying old woman pays her with a bone whistle that hums when the king's name is spoken. The beat is wary tenderness—Lena's loneliness cracked open by the first hint that her silence can't last.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Register
chapters.summary: Still Lena's POV: a customer denounces her, and witch-hunters burn her stall and arrest her neighbor Tam, a deaf tinker who protected her secrets. Interrogated in the palace dungeons, Lena hears something impossible—the king's own voice beneath his guards' laughter, pleading. The emotional beat shifts from fear to horrified resolve as she realizes the hunter-king is also the hunted.

chapters.title: What the Ember Eats
chapters.summary: Alternating between Lena and King Aldric's POV: smuggled into the royal chambers, Lena meets the ember-spirit wearing the crown, which devours memories to stay alive and has nearly emptied its host. With Tam freed and a circle of outcasts assembled, they learn willing memories can starve it—but each offering costs the giver something irreplaceable. The beat is rising sacrifice and desperate love.

chapters.title: The Last Warm Thing
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution in Lena's POV: the binding ritual fails until Lena offers her twelve years of memories of her grandmother, singing the ember into dormancy at last. Aldric wakes diminished but human; Tam and the others become her declared family before the court. Grieving what she gave, Lena carves a new charm—one that holds nothing but hope. The beat is bittersweet renewal.
